source.title: Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders: From Shallow Design to Matching Pursuit
source.authors: Valérie Costa; Thomas Fel; E. Lubana; Bahareh Tolooshams; Demba E. Ba

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own dictionary and active-subset coherence results, refining the geometry claim: shallow SAEs and iterative MP-SAE differ, and MP-SAE's full dictionary and selected subsets have different coherence.
record.gate_note: The paper's statements about sparsity and one-shot inference motivate the work, but are not results by themselves. Expressivity and activation-frequency results are not recorded because they do not directly measure the feature-direction geometry in V1. Coherence values are presented in figures without numerical values in the text; only the qualitative comparisons described by the authors are recorded.
record.test_reason: This is an SAE-methods paper. It compares its MP-SAE with shallow SAEs on reconstruction, activation statistics and dictionary coherence (Babel score). Coherence of a learned SAE dictionary is a property of the SAE, not of a toy network's own feature geometry, so it does not bear on V1. MNIST has no model representation at all, so V4–V5 cannot be tested there. On vision-model features it reports only method-versus-method expressivity and coherence. It does not test whether superposition, polysemanticity or 1-D features hold.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that shallow SAEs implicitly assume quasi-orthogonality, which limits extraction of correlated features. MP-SAE learns a globally coherent dictionary but selects low-redundancy atoms per input. It is more expressive and gives coarse-to-fine hierarchical reconstructions. The MNIST findings are said to generalize to the four vision backbones.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and compares shallow SAE variants with an iterative Matching Pursuit-based SAE, then measures dictionary and selected-subset coherence; it does not reproduce the original toy-model experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The coherence pattern differs between shallow SAEs and MP-SAE, and for MP-SAE between the full dictionary and atoms selected together at inference.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE architectures yield structurally different dictionaries on MNIST: ReLU learns full-digit atoms and the others learn pen strokes. Shallow SAEs are argued to favour near-orthogonal dictionaries because of one-shot inference. On SigLIP, DINOv2, CLIP and ViT features, MP-SAE dictionaries are more coherent than shallow ones (Fig. 3, Figs 5 and 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The geometry (coherence) of recovered dictionary features depends on the SAE's inference architecture. Near-orthogonality of SAE features may partly reflect the encoder's bias rather than the model.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted at Methods and Opportunities at Small Scale (MOSS), ICML 2025
record.problems: The coherence values are only available in figures in the supplied text, with no numerical scores or uncertainty estimates stated. The study does not test the sparsity-dependent transition or the regular geometry of the original toy-model claim.
record.rows_left_out: Expressivity and activation-frequency results (Sections 4 and 7, Figures 2, 4, 7, and 9) were left out because they do not directly measure the feature-direction geometry in V1.

untested.parts: There is no toy network with known sparse features. Sparsity transition, near-orthogonal storage and regular geometry are not tested.
Not tested. SAEs are applied to vision features, but only reconstruction and coherence are compared across methods.
Not tested directly. Stability or canonicity of features across seeds or architectures is not measured on a model's representation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5/V1 tagging is rejected. SAE dictionary coherence is not the toy-model feature geometry that V1 describes, and MNIST pixels are not a network's representation. The paper cites Elhage et al. only as motivation. All coherence values are figure-only. The text's wording on Babel direction is internally inconsistent in Section 7.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the sparsity-dependent transition, regular geometry, or a controlled toy network with a known set of sparse features. The coherence experiments concern learned SAE dictionaries on MNIST and pretrained vision-model representations.

rows.subject: MP-SAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured Babel coherence of the learned dictionary.
rows.measure: Babel score of the full learned dictionary; lower values indicate lower redundancy.
rows.value: figure only; text says MP-SAE has a more coherent dictionary than the shallow SAEs
rows.note: The text describes the dictionary as more coherent than those of shallow SAEs. Exact scores are not stated.
rows.check: This is the Babel coherence of an SAE dictionary trained on raw MNIST pixels. That is a property of the method, not V1's toy-model geometry. It is the study's own method compared with others.

rows.subject: MP-SAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured Babel coherence of atoms selected together at inference.
rows.measure: Babel score of atoms selected at inference; lower values indicate lower redundancy.
rows.baseline: full learned dictionary; shallow SAE selected atoms
rows.value: figure only; text says MP-SAE selects more incoherent atoms at inference than its globally coherent dictionary
rows.note: The text reports a distinction between the full dictionary and the selected subset, but gives no exact scores.
rows.check: This is the coherence of atoms MP-SAE selects at inference, a method property. No superposition version names this quantity.

rows.subject: shallow SAEs (ReLU, JumpReLU, TopK, and BatchTopK)
rows.operation_detail: Measured Babel coherence of the learned dictionaries.
rows.measure: Babel score of full learned dictionaries; lower values indicate lower redundancy.
rows.value: figure only; text says ReLU has the highest coherence among shallow methods and TopK the lowest
rows.note: The text gives the relative ranking within shallow methods and says their dictionary and selected-atom trends align; it does not state whether these dictionaries meet a near-orthogonality threshold.
rows.check: This is the comparator SAEs' dictionary coherence on MNIST pixels. It is a method comparison, not a test of V1.

rows.subject: shallow SAEs (ReLU, JumpReLU, TopK, and BatchTopK)
rows.operation_detail: Measured Babel coherence of atoms selected together at inference.
rows.measure: Babel score of selected atoms; lower values indicate lower redundancy.
rows.baseline: full learned dictionaries; MP-SAE selected atoms
rows.value: figure only; text says shallow-method trends for learned dictionaries and selected atoms align, with ReLU highest and TopK least coherent
rows.note: The reported ordering does not establish whether the selected atoms are nearly orthogonal in absolute terms.
rows.check: This is the comparator SAEs' selected-atom coherence, a method comparison.

rows.subject: MP-SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on SigLIP, DINOv2, CLIP, and ViT representations
rows.operation_detail: Measured Babel coherence of the full learned dictionaries.

conditions.value: SigLIP, DINOv2, CLIP, and ViT (reported together)

rows.measure: Babel score of full dictionaries; lower values indicate lower redundancy.
rows.value: figure only; text says MP-SAE learns globally coherent dictionaries with low Babel scores
rows.note: The paper states that this result generalizes across the evaluated large vision models, but does not give per-backbone scores in the text.
rows.check: This is MP-SAE dictionary coherence on vision-model features, a method property. The baseline should be shallow SAEs: Fig. 8's caption says MP-SAE learns 'more coherent dictionaries'. The text's phrase 'low Babel scores' conflicts with 'more coherent', since a lower score means less redundancy, so the value is ambiguous.

rows.subject: MP-SAE
rows.stage_stated: trained on SigLIP, DINOv2, CLIP, and ViT representations
rows.operation_detail: Measured Babel coherence of subsets of atoms co-activated at inference.

conditions.value: SigLIP, DINOv2, CLIP, and ViT (reported together)

rows.measure: Babel score of co-activated subsets; lower values indicate lower redundancy.
rows.value: figure only; text says inference subsets have higher Babel values than the full dictionaries, indicating local incoherence
rows.note: The paper says the difference between global dictionary coherence and local inference-subset incoherence persists on the large vision models.
rows.check: This is the coherence of co-activated MP-SAE subsets, a method property. The text's wording conflicts: 'higher Babel values' (more redundant) are described as 'local incoherence'.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The authors describe shallow SAEs as favoring near-orthogonal dictionaries, and report that their dictionary and selected-atom coherence trends align; the absolute degree of orthogonality is not given (r3, r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MP-SAE on MNIST and the evaluated large vision-model representations
reader_labels.reason: MP-SAE has a globally coherent dictionary but selects less redundant, locally incoherent subsets at inference, so the geometry depends on whether the full dictionary or active subset is considered (r1, r2, r5, r6).
